summary: Frontend-only E2E testing of the forced-password-change UX. All 7 requested scenarios (9 sub-assertions) passed against the live preview URL. The blocking on-screen popup appears for the forced client user, dashboard is genuinely blocked, all three client-side validations trigger correctly, the server-side wrong-current-password error is surfaced, a successful change transitions the user into the dashboard, re-login with the new password bypasses the force-pw screen, and the seeded admin is never forced (regression clean).
seed_data_creation: Consumed the pre-seeded newclient@test.local — its password is now BrandNew123! and must_change_password flag is cleared. If another forced-flow test is needed, a new editor user must be created via admin Settings > Users.
test_credentials: admin@wifetobe.org / ChangeMe!2026 (regression); newclient@test.local / TempPass123 -> now BrandNew123!
context_for_next_testing_agent: Force-password-change flow is fully verified end-to-end on the preview URL. Validations tested: <8 chars ('Your new password must be at least 8 characters.'), mismatched confirm ('The two new passwords don't match.'), new==current ('Please choose a new password that's different from the temporary one.'), wrong current ('Your current password is incorrect.'). After success, user lands on dashboard (data-testid=logout-btn visible, current-user shows 'newclient@test.local · editor'). newclient@test.local password is now BrandNew123! — recreate a fresh forced user if re-testing this flow.
